agent.problem: The blank asks for the unseen word "demons" in James's sentence. Card 9 gives no basis for reasoning that demons, rather than Romans or Gentiles, believe and shudder, so this tests luck or recall of wording instead of a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: Four of the seven choice cards are discovery guesses without enough context to reason toward an answer: card 2 asks Abraham's identity, card 4 asks what Abraham did, card 8 asks whether he was called God's friend, and card 11 asks what Rahab did. Only cards 6, 9 and 13 offer an informed basis for a pick, so most of this stop's choices are not informed guesses.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
